source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Section 7.2 of the booklet describes a leaf-feeding/sap-sucking insect pest, shown in a photo of a watermelon leaf with pale, whitish speckled/mottled patches consistent with feeding damage from a small sucking insect (leafhopper- or whitefly-type damage). Note: the exact Khmer pest name printed in this section was not clearly legible in the scanned image due to font rendering, so it should be confirmed with a clearer copy of the source or a local extension officer rather than assumed.

According to the source, this pest feeds by sucking plant sap from the leaves, which interferes with the leaf's ability to photosynthesize properly and weakens the plant.

Recommended control measures given: remove and destroy affected leaves showing the damage/webbing by picking them off and disposing of them away from the field; and apply agricultural pesticides, specifically Abamectin or Dinotefuran, to control the pest.
